gallery.title: File:Chester Cathedral interior 002.jpg
gallery.description: Chester Cathedral, font. Italian, given by Earl Egerton of Tatton Park. He believed it was from a C7th BC Etruscan well head. It is now thought to be a C19th reproduction. The two peacocks on the side of Chi-Rho symbol on the side of bowl are an early Christian symbol of new and eternal life given at baptism.

gallery.title: File:Chester Cathedral misericord Hamilton 0146.JPG
gallery.description: Chester Cathedral choir stalls, 1380, detail of a misericord depicting the Madonna and Christ Child with a dove(?) supported by two angels and framed by two pelicans, the symbol of Christ's love for the Church.  The pelican (a mythical bird) was said to pluck feathers from its breast and feed its young on its own blood. The artist has depicted the pelican with a short beak, rather like that of an eagle.

gallery.title: File:Chester Cathedral ext Hamilton 001.JPG
gallery.description: Chester Cathedral, England. The cathedral seen from the south-east looking towards the choir, right, with the Lady Chapel projecting, extreme right, and the south transept, left. The Lady Chapel is in the Early English (or Lancet) Gothic style, marked by the simple windows. The choir is in the late Geometric Decorated Gothic style. The South transept has Flowing Decorated windows in the aisle, and Perpendicular Gothic windows in the clerestory. The friable Red Sandstone building was heavily restored in the 19th century.

gallery.title: File:Chester Cathedral ext Hamilton 005.JPG
gallery.description: Chester Cathedral, England. The cathedral seen from the south-west looking towards the nave, left, and the unusually large south transept, right. The rebuilding of the nave and the building of the south transept commenced in the early 1300s, but ceased, incomplete, in 1375, and did not recommence until about 1485. The different building dates are revealed in the  Flowing Decorated Gothic and Perpendicular Gothic window tracery.

gallery.title: File:Chester Cathedral int Hamilton 024.JPG
gallery.description: Chester Cathedral, England.  The north transept of the cathedral showing a Norman arch and gallery. The North Transept of 2 bays is c1100 with clerestory C15; simple early Norman archway to chapel, now sacristy, east with 6 arches of contemporary triforium above and piscina south; Aspects of the design of the Norman interior are still visible in the north transept, which retains wall arcading and a broadly moulded arch leading to the sacristy, which was formerly a chapel.The transept has retained an early 16th-century coffered ceiling with decorated bosses, two of which are carved with the arms of Henry VIII and Cardinal Wolsey.

gallery.title: File:Westminster Window. adjusted light.JPG
gallery.description: This is two of three modern stained glass windows situated in Chester Cathedral.This window was commissioned in 1992 and was given by the Duke of Westminster. It is a replacement window as the original was damaged during enemy action over Chester in the 2nd World War. Some of the glass from the original has been incorporated into the design.
